toxicity:

tips:

care:

P_NAME: Hibiscus, Gudhal Flower (Hybrid, Any Color) - Plant
P_DESC:
manage:
Hibiscus plants need plenty of water and like their soil to be consistently moist, but never soggy. You can check the soil's moisture by touching it. If it feels dry and crusty, your plants need to be watered. If the soil feels soft and damp to the touch, you don't need to water your plants that day.

P_NAME: Hibiscus Set of 3 Different Color Plant
P_DESC:
Tropical Hibiscus:
Tropical hibiscus plants should be kept consistently moist, so water whenever the top inch of soil is dry. (Stick your finger in the soil to check.) Containers may need to be watered 3 to 4 times weekly at the beginning of the summer and daily toward the end of the summer as the plants grow.

P_NAME: Fiesta Hibiscus All Time Flowering Live Plant with Flower
P_DESC:
Light:
Provide your plant full sunlight (6 to 8 hours). Over winter, bring your hibiscus inside and place it by a south facing window for maximum sunlight. Lots of light is needed for the best blooms.
Water:
Water your hibiscus a lot over spring and summer.

Planting Location:
Sunny spot with well-draining, slightly acidic soil.
Planting Method:
 Seeds:
Soak overnight, plant 1/4 inch deep.
 Cuttings: Use 4-6 inch cuttings with rooting hormone.
 Watering:
Keep soil consistently moist, not waterlogged.

Cultivation and Care:
While the blue hibiscus is relatively drought-tolerant once established, consistent watering is essential during its initial growth phases.Not watering the plant on time can cause the flowers to wilt and dry. Only water the plant when the soil becomes noticeably dry.

Fertilizer: 
Hibiscus plants benefit from regular fertilizer applications, especially if they are grown in containers. Slow-release fertilizers or liquid fertilizers with high phosphorus can help the plant grow stronger and produce more blooms.
 Location:
Hibiscus plants can be grown in containers or in the ground. If you live in a windy area, choose a protected location for your plant.

P_DESC:
Light:
Hibiscus plants thrive in full sun, needing at least 6-8 hours of direct sunlight daily to promote abundant flowering.
Soil:
Well-draining soil is crucial.
Water:
These plants require consistent moisture but should not be waterlogged.

Choose a sunny location: 
Hibiscus plants prefer full sun.
 Consider the weather:
The weather affects the color of your hibiscus flowers. In hot, sunny weather, the flowers will be brighter oranges and reds. When the weather cools down, the colors will become softer oranges and yellows.

soil:
Hibiscus plants prefer slightly acidic, well-drained soil. You can mix in some loam to improve the soil. If you're growing your hibiscus in a container, make sure it has drainage holes.
watering:
Water your hibiscus plant regularly and thoroughly. If it's in a pot, water it until water comes out of the bottom hole.

Fertilizing: 
Use a water-soluble fertilizer in combination with a slow-release type. You can also use a complete fertilizer every two to three weeks from April to September. 
Repotting:
Repot your hibiscus every couple of years in early spring. Use a pot that is wide but relatively shallow, and avoid deep pots.

tips:
Hardy Hibiscus thrives best in well drained soil, amended with organic matter. Hibiscus prefers acidic soil. To add acidity to your soil, add Peat moss or potting soil to your garden. If your soil is mostly clay, consider planting Hibiscus in a raised bed, this helps to eliminate water buildup.
